Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

Closing by choice after design review. The embedded consumer that motivated this never needed per-session GET enrichment: its check-then-act call sites dissolve into #44766's `{ interrupted }` result (idle interrupt is a documented no-op), and the remaining liveness need (admission routing) is served fine by `sessions.active()` membership in-process. Gluing process-local runtime state onto the session GET response — even quarantined in a separate `GetInfo` type — muddles durable and runtime lifetimes for no consumer. If a remote consumer ever needs per-session runtime status, a dedicated `session.status` endpoint is the right shape, argued from that consumer's requirements.

I reproduced this and isolated the failing path further.

Environment:

* Windows 11
* OpenCode Go
* Model: `muse-spark-1.2-contributor`
* OpenCodex 2.32.0
* Codex Desktop
* Same OpenCode Go API key for all tests

Results:

1. Muse works normally inside the OpenCode app.

2. Direct request to the Responses API works:

`POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses`

with:

`model: muse-spark-1.2-contributor`

Result:

`HTTP 200`
`status: completed`

So the model, account, API key and OpenCode Go access are all working.

3. The same model routed through the Chat Completions protocol fails consistently:

`/v1/chat/completions`

Result:

`HTTP 500`
`Internal server error`

4. OpenCodex debug confirms the failing request is using:

`adapter: openai-chat`
`model: muse-spark-1.2-contributor`
`stream: true`

5. After a completely fresh OpenCodex 2.32.0 reinstall, other models through the same setup work correctly:

* GPT-5.6 Luna: 200
* DeepSeek V4 Flash: 200
* Gemini 3.7 Flash: 200
* Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor: 500

This therefore appears isolated to Muse + the Chat Completions API path.

The OpenCode Go documentation currently lists Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor under `/v1/responses`, and our direct test confirms that endpoint works.

Possible fixes:

* Make `muse-spark-1.2-contributor` work correctly through `/v1/chat/completions`, or
* Return a clear 4xx unsupported-protocol error instead of HTTP 500 when Muse is called through Chat Completions, and
* Ensure clients can reliably discover that this model requires the Responses API.

This also seems related to the existing Muse Chat Completions streaming/schema issues, but in this case the request fails immediately with HTTP 500 before a usable response is returned.

Round-two findings — all addressed in the latest push, within the app-only constraint:

**[P1] Do not clone optimistic payloads** — Fixed by removing the merge entirely. `rebuildQueue` now waits (`settledPendingList`, bounded retries) until every locally queued row is visible in the authoritative pending list or has left the local store, and rewrites against authoritative payloads only. A rewrite can no longer clone a lossy optimistic row or duplicate an in-flight original; if admissions never settle, the rewrite aborts with a toast and the edit stays open.

**[P1] Only roll back clones after a verified delivery conflict** — Fixed. `cancelQueued` classifies outcomes: success → cancelled; a tagged 409 `ConflictError` body → delivered; anything else (transport, lost response) → one retry, then "failed". Clones are withdrawn only on a *verified* delivery conflict, and only when they are unchanged copies — an edited clone stays because the edit is still wanted. Unverifiable cancellations keep both copies (duplicate is recoverable, silent loss is not) and surface a toast; the closing sync renders reality.

**[P1] Preserve queued model and agent selection** — Commands fixed to match prompts: `sendCommand` omits `agent`/`model` for queue deliveries, so a queued slash command no longer reconfigures the running turn server-side. Applying a *recorded* selection at promotion time genuinely needs the server to honor per-item selection during inbox promotion — out of scope for this app-only PR, flagged as the follow-up.

**[P1] Handle failure when cancelling an edited steer's original** — Fixed. The steer's original is cancelled through `cancelQueued`: verified conflict means the original already ran (accepted mid-edit-delivery case); an unverifiable failure raises a toast and leaves the original visible in the panel for manual removal instead of being silently ignored.

**[P1] Make revert and inbox cancellation one server-side boundary** — Agreed that the complete fix is server-side; noted in the code as the follow-up. Client-side the sweep now uses a `timeCreated` cutoff captured at stage success, so the asynchronous list response can no longer cancel a prompt admitted after the revert; the remaining gap is an old admission still in flight when the list is fetched.

**[P2] Keep the edit stash until confirmation succeeds** — Fixed by inverting the flow: the stash is restored only after the confirmation lands. A failed confirmation keeps the edit open with the edited content still in the composer (correct mode included), so nothing is overwritten or lost and Enter retries. The `recoverText` overwrite is gone.

**[P2] Preserve or disable rich content during queue edits** — Preserved. Confirming an edit now builds a real prompt request from the composer content (`buildPromptRequest`): images added during the edit are uploaded as data URIs, mentions are parsed structurally, the original's stored attachments are re-attached, and the model-visible comment notes survive as before. Ambient composer context (open review comments) deliberately stays out of a queued edit — it belongs to the next fresh prompt.

**[P2] Do not merge a stale local queue row over an authoritative steer** — Resolved by construction: with the merge removed, a row another client steered shows up in the settled authoritative list with steer delivery and simply drops out of the rewrite; it is never cloned or cancelled.

Full queue suite (8 e2e) green, composer unit tests green, full app suite re-run green.

Thanks for the report. I checked the behavior against the reported v1.18.21 source. OpenCode does not include the remaining context or a “will this task fit?” estimate in the model-visible system prompt or messages. Its bundled agent prompt instead tells the agent to persist and complete requested work.

Automatic compaction is enabled by default. After a completed response reaches the model’s usable context threshold, core creates a structured continuation summary, retains a recent tail of the conversation, and sends a synthetic continuation prompt. Plugins can transform the system prompt/messages and compaction behavior, and project instructions or a custom agent can also change model behavior, but the report does not include the model, exact refusal text, session, configuration, or instructions needed to identify which input produced this response.

Closing because the reported preemptive refusal is not a core behavior we can reproduce from these steps. If this is reproducible with a clean configuration, please provide the exact model/provider, exact prompt and response, an exported or shared affected session, and the relevant configuration/instruction files.

Round-three triage. This round splits into deterministic bugs (fixed) and race-window enumerations that a client cannot close against these APIs (declined or noted as server-side follow-ups) — further client-side compensation machinery is what created several of these windows in the first place.

**Fixed (deterministic):**

- **Preserve original agent/skill attachments** — editing degrades structured mentions to plain text; original agent and skill references now survive the edit as long as their mention text still appears in the edited prompt, alongside newly typed structured mentions.
- **Image-only edited prompts** — confirmation now treats a prompt with images as non-empty instead of silently discarding the edit.
- **Command-configured selection** — solved with one guard: slash commands always steer (`delivery: "steer"`), which is exactly the pre-PR v2 behavior. Commands can carry server-applied configuration at admission, so they are simply never queued.
- **Cancellation retry deleting the only prompt** — the retry (added last round) created this window; it is removed. One attempt, classified, done.

**Declined / follow-ups:**

- **Idempotent edit-confirmation retries** — requires a lost success response followed by a manual retry; the closing sync renders server reality between attempts. Accepted as vanishingly rare rather than adding client-side idempotency bookkeeping.
- **Apply queued selection at delivery** and **revert/inbox boundary** — both genuinely need server support (per-item selection at promotion; a revert-discards-inbox rule). Flagged as server-side follow-ups; this PR is intentionally app-only.
- **Concurrently steered item cancelled by a rebuild** — requires a second client steering the same item inside the rewrite's snapshot-to-cancel window. Accepted.

Also rebased onto latest `v2` (conflict resolved) so CI can run. Queue suite 8/8, composer units green, typecheck clean.

I see #40956 addresses the same issue (#40955) and was opened earlier — happy to close this one in favor of that if maintainers prefer.

Two differences in the check used here, flagging for whoever reviews either:

- **Parent-chain vs ID ordering**: this PR asks "did the newest user message get an assistant child" (`assistant.parentID === lastUser.id`), which is robust for imported sessions where message IDs aren't monotonic (same reason `MessageV2.isAfter` compares `time.created` before IDs). #40956 compares `lastUser.id > lastAssistant.id` directly.
- **Synthetic-only messages**: this PR skips restart when the newest user message has only synthetic parts (e.g. workspace move/warp reminders sent with `noReply`), which must never produce a reply.

Otherwise the approaches are equivalent: both restart the loop after cancel settles, and both preserve bare-cancel semantics.

Also heads-up: this PR adds a test only for the resume path; #40956 additionally pins the "bare cancel does not restart the loop" behavior, which is worth having on whichever PR lands.

Update: the `bare cancel does not restart the loop` pin is now included here too (`cancel without queued input does not restart the loop`), alongside the resume regression test. Verified stable across repeated runs locally.

Round-four triage — final position for this PR.

**Taken:** queued move/compaction/synthetic items are now treated as ordering barriers: a rewrite aborts and leaves the queue untouched instead of reordering prompts around a control item (2-line guard).

**Everything else is declined for this PR, deliberately.** Six of the ten findings re-raise items already resolved as declined or as server-side follow-ups (per-item selection at promotion, revert-inbox boundary, lost-response idempotency, concurrent-client races, withdrawal verification). The command finding reverses the previous round's: round three flagged that queueing a command reconfigures the running turn, this round flags the fix for that — and correctly notes the actual answer is server-side command handling. There is no client-side resolution to choose from, only two imperfect behaviors; commands-always-steer matches pre-PR v2 exactly and keeps the running turn intact, so it stays.

The remaining windows share one shape: they simulate atomicity the inbox API does not offer, and each client-side compensation layer manufactures the next review round's findings (this round's withdrawal-verification finding is a hole in round two's compensation, which was itself a fix for round one's). The durable fix is a small server surface — inbox reorder/edit endpoints, per-item selection honored at promotion, and a revert-discards-inbox rule — at which point most of the client scaffolding here (settledPendingList, cancelQueued, clone withdrawal) gets deleted, not extended. That is the follow-up worth doing; more client machinery is not.

Feature has been manually tested end to end; queue suite is 8/8 e2e plus storybook visual states matched against the Figma comps.

## Additional family-wide boundary evidence

I repeated the adjacent-boundary experiment for the remaining GPT-5.6 routes on the same account and date.

Each request used:

- ChatGPT OAuth
- An isolated `OPENCODE_DB`
- `opencode run --pure`
- Automatic compaction and pruning disabled
- Project configuration disabled
- A one-step agent with tools denied
- Deterministic repeated ` x` payloads
- Separate databases for every request

| OpenCode model | Backend model/route | 921,858 input | Adjacent 921,859 target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | Accepted | `ContextOverflowError` |
| `gpt-5.6-terra` | `gpt-5.6-terra` | Accepted | `ContextOverflowError` |
| `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-5.6-luna` | Accepted | `ContextOverflowError` |
| `gpt-5.6-luna-fast` | `gpt-5.6-luna`, priority service tier | Accepted | `ContextOverflowError` |

Every accepted request reported:

```text
input:    921,858
output:   5
finish:   stop
response: OK
```

Every adjacent request returned `ContextOverflowError`. Rejected responses did not include usage metadata, so the 921,859 target is inferred from an otherwise identical deterministic payload containing exactly one additional token.

Across all probe databases:

```text
compaction markers: 0
normal OpenCode database probe sessions: 0
```

The official Sol, Terra, and Luna model cards all advertise the same envelope:

```text
context: 1,050,000
input:     922,000
output:    128,000
```

`gpt-5.6-luna-fast` is an OpenCode-generated priority-service route whose API model remains `gpt-5.6-luna`; it is not a separate OpenAI model.

This strengthens the original finding: for this tested account, OAuth route, originator, and date, the Codex 272k/372k client budgets do not represent the endpoint capacity for any routed GPT-5.6 model.

It still does not establish that every account, plan, originator, or rollout cohort receives the same capacity. This is why a route-aware limit or supported explicit override remains preferable to another universal hardcoded value.

Confirming this on **Intel**, not just AMD Zen 3 — and still present 16 releases later.

### Environment
- opencode `1.18.21` (crashes) / `1.18.22` (currently installed, auto-updated)
- Bun `1.3.14` (bundled), binary 184,498,304 bytes
- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel `7.0.0-30-generic`, x86_64
- CPU: **Intel Core i9-14900KF** (Raptor Lake), microcode `0x133`
- Installed via npm (`~/.opencode/bin/opencode`), not the desktop package

### CPU lacks AVX-512
```
avx512f  : absent
avx512bw : absent
avx512vl : absent
avx2     : present
```

This matters for scope: **every Intel consumer CPU from 12th gen onward lacks AVX-512**
(disabled because of the E-cores). So this is not an AMD-specific bucket — it covers
Alder Lake, Raptor Lake, and Meteor Lake desktops/laptops as well as Zen 3.

### Same evidence in the npm binary
Disassembling `.text` of the installed binary:
```
%zmm register uses    : 6888
%k1-%k7 mask registers: 2575
```
Concrete EVEX instructions present:
```
vbroadcasti32x4 -0x22b9e5f(%rip),%zmm5
vinserti64x4    $0x1,%ymm3,%zmm4,%zmm3
vshufi64x2      $0x0,%zmm4,%zmm4,%zmm4
```

### Kernel traps
Two crashes, **the same instruction pointer**, different threads and different model
providers:
```
Aug 23 18:10:22 kernel: traps: HeapHelper[504903] trap invalid opcode
  ip:2607064 sp:7217591ec8d0 error:0 in opencode[21a3064,24c8000+36e6000]

Aug 24 16:04:32 kernel: traps: opencode[3915644] trap invalid opcode
  ip:2607064 sp:7ffd19044c90 error:0 in opencode[21a3064,24c8000+36e6000]
```
Crash 1 was on a local Ollama provider, crash 2 on a remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint,
so it is below the provider layer — consistent with what #33595 argues.

### One difference worth noting
For us this is **intermittent, not every session**: 2 crashes in roughly 40 hours of
heavy agentic use, both during long tool-call loops, rather than a crash on every start.
That fits a rarely-taken code path containing AVX-512 rather than a hot one.

Possibly related on the same host: `opencode run` twice hung indefinitely with no output
and no upstream request ever sent (once ~19 minutes, zero completed turns, model server
idle with nothing loaded) and had to be killed. No log line after the run started. Not
claiming it is the same defect, only that it appeared on the same build.

Ruled out here: system OOM (55 GiB free at crash 1), machine fault (the later reboot was
a clean `systemd-reboot`), and the Raptor Lake Vmin-shift errata (microcode `0x133`,
zero MCEs).

Happy to attach a full backtrace — `systemd-coredump` is now capturing cores on this host
with `ProcessSizeMax=16G`, so the next occurrence on `1.18.22` will produce one.
